onenight.title: Une nuit
onenight.kicker: One night ashore · pick the quarter you are berthed nearest · walking order
onenight.lede: Barcelona eats late: a vermut or a glass from seven, the table from nine, the music after eleven, and the clubs do not start until past midnight. Each quarter below is one evening, in the order you walk it. Every name opens its full card; hours were re-checked on 15 October 2026, and where the listings disagree the step says call.
onenight.door_en: Crew ashore for one evening: a plan for each quarter — the glass, the counter, the table and the late room, in walking order.
onenight.door_note: Le verre · le comptoir · la table · la nuit

quarters.name: El Born and La Ribera
quarters.line: The house fizz of 1929, the counter with no menu, natural wine to one in the morning.

steps.name: El Xampanyet
steps.text: A glass of the cloudy house xampanyet and the anchovies at the tiled bar on Carrer de Montcada. Walk in; listings give Tuesday to Saturday evenings, closed Monday and August, and they disagree on Sunday: check.

steps.name: Cal Pep
steps.text: Round the corner to Plaça de les Olles and the counter where the cooks choose your plates. The counter is walk-in only, so queue; dinner runs to about 23:30 Tuesday to Saturday by a May 2026 listing, with Monday dinner only: call.

steps.name: Can Cisa / Bar Brutal
steps.text: Up to Carrer de la Barra de Ferro for a natural glass from one of the deepest lists in the city. Time Out gives Tuesday to Saturday to one in the morning; another listing differs: check.

quarters.after: Cheaper: the dozen-seat cave at [[card:Bar Zim|Bar Zim]], across Via Laietana, cash only. Earlier: the Picasso Museum on the same street keeps its own hours ([[card:Museu Picasso|its card]]).

quarters.name: El Raval
quarters.line: The long bar over the open kitchen, a jazz set in a narrow bar, absinthe to finish.

steps.name: Bar Cañete
steps.text: Take a stool at the long bar over the kitchen on Carrer de la Unió and order the tortillitas de camarón. Monday to Saturday, closed Sunday; the stools are walk-in with a queue, tables are booked.

steps.name: 23 Robadors
steps.text: Five minutes to Carrer d'en Robador and the scruffy bar with two live sets most nights: a small door charge paid on the night, no bookings, open to two (three at the weekend) by Time Out.

steps.name: Bar Marsella
steps.text: Down Carrer de Sant Pau to the absinthe room, reputedly of 1820: sugar cube, fork, iced water. Its posted hours vary between sources, so it may be shut on your night.

quarters.after: Spend more: [[venue:v15-suculent|Suculent]] on the Rambla del Raval, for the tartare on marrow bone (the listings disagree on its days: call). For a cocktail instead of absinthe, the trapeze bar at [[card:London Bar|London Bar]].

quarters.name: Barri Gòtic
quarters.line: Four tapas since 1945, the dining room of 1786, jazz under the arches of the Plaça Reial.

steps.name: Bar La Plata
steps.text: Stand at the marble counter on Carrer de la Mercè for the fried fish, the anchovies and a glass from the barrel. Not re-confirmed this autumn; listings give evenings Monday to Saturday from 18:00 or 18:30: check.

steps.name: Can Culleretes
steps.text: Ten minutes to Carrer d'en Quintana and the city's oldest dining room for the canelons and the crema catalana. Time Out gives dinner Tuesday to Saturday from 20:00, Sunday lunch only, closed Monday.

steps.name: Jamboree
steps.text: Round the corner to the vaulted cellar on the Plaça Reial for the first set; tickets for named acts about EUR 16–20, and the club takes over late.

quarters.name: Barceloneta and the port
quarters.line: The sand at sundown, the beer hall of 1962, the rice house of 1836.

steps.name: Barceloneta beach
steps.text: Walk out of the fishermen's grid onto the sand as the light goes; keep your phone on you.

steps.name: El Vaso de Oro
steps.text: Back into the grid to Carrer de Balboa and the narrow standing beer hall: a caña and the solomillo with foie. Not re-confirmed this autumn; listings give daily to midnight.

steps.name: 7 Portes
steps.text: Ten minutes along the Passeig d'Isabel II to the arcades and the rice with every shell already taken off. Open every day; the city listing gives to midnight, others to one: book for a group.

quarters.after: Come back at lunchtime for the bomba where it was born, [[venue:v12-la-cova-fumada|La Cova Fumada]]: it is a daytime kitchen, evenings Thursday and Friday only, closed Sunday.

quarters.name: Sant Antoni and Poble Sec
quarters.line: Wine at shelf price, the montadito counter, the pintxo street, the old ballroom at half past midnight.

steps.name: Els Sortidors del Parlament
steps.text: A bottle at shelf price plus corkage under the garage arches of Carrer del Parlament. Listings give weekdays from 17:00; one older record says closed Tuesday: check.

steps.name: Quimet & Quimet
steps.text: Across the Paral·lel to Poeta Cabanyes for the salmon and truffled-honey montadito, standing. Weekdays only by Time Out (to 22:30), closed at the weekend and in August.

steps.name: Carrer de Blai
steps.text: Two streets on, the pedestrian pintxo street: a skewer or two at about EUR 1.80–2.50 each, cash.

steps.name: Sala Apolo and Nitsa
steps.text: On Friday and Saturday only: Nitsa in the 1940s ballroom on Nou de la Rambla, about half past midnight to six.

quarters.after: Spend more: Albert Adrià's [[venue:v03-enigma|Enigma]] on the Sant Antoni side, booked well ahead (the listings disagree on its nights).

quarters.name: Gràcia
quarters.line: Natural wine on tap, a Bib Gourmand menu, records on a hand-built system.

steps.name: Bar Salvatge
steps.text: Carrer de Verdi and eight rotating taps of natural wine with a cheese board; open most evenings from 19:00.

steps.name: Oníric
steps.text: The Bib Gourmand room: a tasting menu between about EUR 18 and 36 by the sitting. Listings give Tuesday to Saturday: book, and confirm the night.

steps.name: Oblicuo Hi-Fi Bar
steps.text: Down to Riera de Sant Miquel for a sake while the record plays; open to three at the weekend by its listings.

quarters.after: Earlier, at noon: the 1954 vermut bodega [[venue:vc-bar-bodega-quimet|Bar Bodega Quimet]], whose hours we could not re-read this autumn.

quarters.name: The Eixample
quarters.line: The vermut of 2007, three hundred bottles at the counter, Gaudí's roof by night.

steps.name: Morro Fi
steps.text: Standing vermut at the bar that remade the ritual; Monday to Thursday to 23:00, Friday and Saturday all day, closed Sunday (May 2026 listing).

steps.name: Bar Mut
steps.text: A taxi up to Pau Claris and the wine-first room: book, it fills fast, and the hours were not re-read this autumn.

steps.name: Casa Batlló & La Pedrera
steps.text: Walk down the Passeig de Gràcia past the two Gaudí houses lit at night; both run night sessions on some evenings, booked on their own sites.

quarters.after: Spend more: a counter of the new guard at [[venue:vr-kamikaze|Kamikaze]], this year's first star (Tuesday to Saturday by MICHELIN's listing), or the self-taught chef's two stars at [[venue:v08-cinc-sentits|Cinc Sentits]].

quarters.name: Poblenou
quarters.line: The quiet sand, the suquet under the ombú tree, natural wine on the rambla.

steps.name: Bogatell
steps.text: The beach where the city's own people swim after work; walk it as the light goes.

steps.name: Els Pescadors
steps.text: Up to Plaça de Prim for the suquet and the rice on the terrace. Every day, dinner from about 20:00 by the May 2026 listing: book the terrace.

steps.name: Amateur Bar
steps.text: Ten minutes to Carrer de Llull for a natural glass; listings disagree on its hours, so check before you walk.

getaway.title: Le week-end
getaway.door_en: Friday night to Sunday afternoon: the Born at the counter, the Gothic before nine, the market and the long bar, Gaudí's park at the end of the day, and a Sunday of vermut and rice by the sea.
getaway.door_note: Le comptoir · le marché · Gaudí · la mer
getaway.kicker: The getaway weekend · Friday night to Sunday afternoon
getaway.lede: Barcelona sells itself as a boulevard of terraces, a photo-menu paella and a queue at the basilica. The real weekend is the counter, the market and the noon vermut: the Born's bars on Friday night, the Gothic before the crowds, the Boqueria before eleven, a long lunch at the bar over an open kitchen, Gaudí's park in the late light, and Sunday at the sea with the rice. Every stop below is already in this guide and was re-checked on 15 October 2026; where a place could not be re-confirmed, the stop says so. This reading puts them in order, and tells you what to book before you fly.
book: [[card:Park Güell from the back entrance|Park Güell]] — a timed Monumental Zone ticket for Saturday afternoon, online only: €18 (Oct 2026).
[[venue:v07-bar-ca-ete|Bar Cañete]] — a table for Saturday lunch, or plan to queue for the counter stools.
[[venue:v05-mont-bar|Mont Bar]] — Saturday dinner; the snacks are the reason to come.
[[venue:v14-els-pescadors|Els Pescadors]] — the terrace for Sunday lunch.

stops.name: The house fizz at El Xampanyet
stops.text: Start where the bar took its name from its own sparkling wine in 1929: a glass and the anchovies, standing.
stops.meta: Carrer de Montcada 22 · walk-in · evenings Tue–Sat by listings, closed Mon and August · check

stops.name: The seafood counter at Cal Pep
stops.text: No menu: the cooks decide. Let them, and ask for the tortilla and whatever came in that morning.
stops.meta: Plaça de les Olles 8 · counter walk-in only · dinner to about 23:30 Tue–Sat (May 2026) · call

stops.name: A natural glass at Can Cisa / Bar Brutal
stops.text: The bottle shop at the door and the bar behind it, for one last glass from Catalan growers.
stops.meta: Barra de Ferro 1 · to 01:00 Tue–Sat by Time Out · check

days.label: Saturday
days.title: The old town early, Gaudí late

stops.name: The Gothic Quarter before nine
stops.text: From the Plaça Reial to the cathedral and the Roman walls while the lanes are empty; the shrapnel scars in Sant Felip Neri.
stops.meta: About 1 km · 30 minutes, longer with stops

stops.name: The Boqueria before eleven
stops.text: In past the front stalls to the back rows for cheese, ham and the Escala anchovies, before the lunchtime crush.

stops.name: A suizo at Granja M. Viader
stops.text: Two streets away, the spoon-thick hot chocolate under cream in the room that says it invented Cacaolat.

stops.name: Lunch at the long bar of Bar Cañete
stops.text: The bar over the open kitchen: the tortillitas de camarón and whatever the counter is cooking.
stops.meta: Carrer de la Unió 17 · Mon–Sat, closed Sun · book a table or queue for the bar

stops.name: Park Güell from the back gate
stops.ref: card:Park Güell from the back entrance
stops.text: Taxi or metro up to the Carretera del Carmel entrance and walk down through the park to the terrace on your timed ticket.
stops.meta: About 1.5 hours · €18 timed ticket (Oct 2026) · winter hours shorten

stops.name: Dinner at Mont Bar
stops.text: Two stars since November 2025, and the snacks are the point: order at least three and let the kitchen lead.

stops.name: Records at Oblicuo Hi-Fi Bar
stops.text: A taxi to Gràcia and a sake while the selector plays a record through the hand-built system.
stops.meta: Riera de Sant Miquel 59 · to 03:00 at the weekend by listings

stops.name: The Sunday book market at Sant Antoni
stops.text: Old books, cards and stamps round the iron market on Sunday morning, as the city has done for decades.

stops.name: Fer el vermut at Els Sortidors del Parlament
stops.text: Round the corner, the noon vermut under the garage arches with olives and a tin; this is what the city does with a Sunday.
stops.meta: Carrer del Parlament · Fri–Sun from 12:00 by its listing · check

stops.name: Rice under the ombú at Els Pescadors
stops.text: A taxi to Poblenou and Plaça de Prim for the suquet or the rice on the terrace.
stops.meta: Plaça de Prim 1 · daily 13:00–16:00 (May 2026) · book the terrace

stops.name: A walk on Bogatell
stops.text: Down to the quiet end of the city beach to walk the lunch off before the airport.

more.title: If you have only one evening
more.text: The Raval: the counter at [[venue:v07-bar-ca-ete|Bar Cañete]], a set at [[card:23 Robadors|23 Robadors]], and absinthe at [[card:Bar Marsella|Bar Marsella]]. That is the city in one night.

more.title: The grand night instead
more.text: Swap Saturday's dinner for one of the three-star houses: [[venue:v01-disfrutar|Disfrutar]], the 2024 world No. 1, books about a year ahead; [[venue:v04-cocina-hermanos-torres|Cocina Hermanos Torres]] and [[venue:v02-lasarte|Lasarte]] take bookings months out. Confirm the day: their published service days disagree.

more.title: Or the mountain instead of the park
more.text: Take Saturday out of town: [[card:Montserrat|Montserrat]] is about 1h20 by train and rack railway from Plaça Espanya. The Escolania sings at 13:00 on weekdays and 12:00 on Sundays, never on Saturdays.

more.title: This October and November
items: 48h Open House BCN opens buildings that are usually shut on 24–25 October: [[card:48h Open House BCN, 24–25 October|its card]].
Clocks go back an hour in the early hours of Sunday 25 October.
All Saints on 1 November is the Castanyada: chestnuts, sweet potatoes and panellets ([[card:The Castanyada: chestnuts, panellets, moniatos|its card]]); many kitchens close for the holiday.
Verdi's Requiem at the Liceu on 3–4 November, and the 58th Barcelona Jazz Festival through November ([[card:The Barcelona Jazz Festival, 58th edition|its card]]).
The MICHELIN Guide Spain 2027 is announced on Tuesday 24 November, in Huesca: the three-star list may move.

more.title: Where to sleep
more.text: This guide does not judge hotels. The weekend is built to be walked from the Born, the Gothic or the Eixample. The hotels in it are ones we send you to for something else: the Casa Fuster for [[card:Café Vienès, Casa Fuster|its café]], [[card:Casa Bonay & Satan's Coffee Corner|Casa Bonay]] for its coffee, and the EDITION and Sir Victor for their roofs. We have not judged their rooms.

more.title: What we would leave out
more.text: A meal on La Rambla itself, and any paella with a photo menu ([[card:Restaurants on La Rambla|the warning]]). Turning up at Park Güell or the Sagrada Família without a timed ticket. And August, when the family kitchens close and the city empties of its own people.
